1: # ScratchLab — Browser DJ Booth
2: 
3: A two-deck browser DJ app with a real signed-rate scratch engine, Web MIDI controller support, capacitive platter detection, and drag-and-drop MP3 import. No build step, no uploads — audio stays on the device.
4: 
5: ## Run it
6: 
7: ```bash
8: # from this repository root
9: python3 -m http.server 3002
10: # or use the project start script
11: ./start.sh
12: ```
13: 
14: Open <http://localhost:3002>. Chrome or Edge is recommended for Web MIDI. Click anywhere once (or the audio chip) to resume the audio context.
15: 
16: ## Highlights
17: 
18: - **Real jog-wheel scratching** — an AudioWorklet moves an interpolated read-head at signed rates, so reverse scratches, pitch bends, and touch-to-scratch feel immediate. A plain `AudioBufferSourceNode` cannot play backwards reliably.
19: - **Import your own MP3s** — use **IMPORT MP3** or drag audio files onto the page. Files are decoded locally, analysed for BPM, rendered in the library, and loaded to a deck instantly.
20: - **Web MIDI input** — notes, CCs, pitch bend, aftertouch, program changes, and clock/sysex are parsed. A live monitor shows every incoming message and decoded jog delta.
21: - **Capacitive vs non-touch platters** — mapping a touch note marks the deck `CAPACITIVE`. In **AUTO** mode, capacitive decks scratch only while touched and pitch-nudge when released; non-touch decks auto-grab on rotation and release after the wheel stops.
22: - **Relative decoder modes** — 7-bit two's complement (`64 = 0`), offset, signed-bit, and absolute delta modes, plus adjustable ticks-per-revolution and sensitivity.
23: - **MIDI Learn and guided auto-map** — bind any control from MIDI Setup, or run the wizard and move each control once.
24: - **Virtual MIDI controller** — test the full MIDI path without hardware; it feeds the same parser as a physical controller.
25: - **Two full decks** — play/cue, sync, loops, four hot cues, tempo, 3-band EQ, filter, echo, channel faders, crossfader, master volume, waveforms, and VU meters.
26: - **Four demo tracks** — procedurally generated so the app is playable before importing anything.
27: 
28: ## Default virtual-controller mapping
29: 
30: | Control | Deck A | Deck B |
31: | --- | --- | --- |
32: | Jog (relative CC) | CH 16 · CC 100 | CH 16 · CC 101 |
33: | Touch sensor (note) | CH 16 · Note 60 | CH 16 · Note 61 |
34: | Play | CH 16 · Note 70 | CH 16 · Note 71 |
35: | Cue | CH 16 · Note 72 | CH 16 · Note 73 |
36: | Hot cues 1–4 | Notes 80–83 | Notes 84–87 |
37: 
38: Crossfader: **CH 16 · CC 7**.
39: 
40: ## Keyboard shortcuts
41: 
42: - `Space` / `A` — play or pause Deck A
43: - `L` — play or pause Deck B
44: - `S` / `;` — cue Deck A / Deck B
45: - `Q` / `E` — scratch Deck A backwards / forwards
46: - `O` / `P` — scratch Deck B backwards / forwards
47: - `←` / `→` — move the crossfader
48: - `Esc` — close the topmost panel
49: 
50: ## Tests
51: 
52: ```bash
53: node --test tests/*.test.mjs
54: ```
55: 
56: The tests cover MIDI parsing, relative-jog decoding modes, BPM estimation, waveform peaks, and display formatting.
57: 
58: ## Notes and assumptions
59: 
60: - MP3/audio decoding uses the browser's `decodeAudioData`; support follows the browser codec list.
61: - MIDI Learn is used instead of hardcoded controller profiles because jog CCs, touch notes, and channels vary between manufacturers.
62: - The default relative encoding is 7-bit two's complement (`64 = 0`). If your wheel turns the wrong way or feels too sensitive, change **Encoder type**, **Ticks per revolution**, or **Scratch sensitivity** in MIDI Setup.
63: - Beat detection is best-effort analysis for imported files; manually verified BPMs are not required for scratching or playback.
64: - MIDI mappings, platter settings, and hot cues persist in `localStorage`.

- Enable MIDI support for the Numark Party Mix Live in the existing ScratchLab browser DJ app.

- Apply the change without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them when finished.
- Update the existing game, which is already playable.

- Use the existing MIDI Learn and mapping framework; investigate a controller-specific preset for easier setup.

### Completed
- Inspected the existing MIDI manager, MIDI parsing, setup UI, auto-map wizard, tests, and README.
- Found an upstream Mixxx Numark Party Mix mapping that lists jog wheel CC 6 on channels 1 and 2, crossfader CC 8, deck controls, and other control messages.

### Active
- Implement and verify Numark Party Mix Live support.

### Blocked
- DuckDuckGo search could not run because `uvx` is unavailable; no code changes have been made.

1. Add a controller-specific mapping/profile based on verified Party Mix Live MIDI messages, with a reasonable fallback to MIDI Learn.
2. Add tests for the profile and MIDI manager behavior.
3. Update setup guidance and README, then run tests and perform a browser check with a small JPEG screenshot.

- `js/midi.js`: MIDI bindings, device discovery, and control dispatch.
- `js/midi-core.js`: MIDI parsing and jog decoding.
- `js/app.js`: setup UI behavior and controller control handling.
- `index.html`: MIDI setup and controller mapping interface.
- `tests/midi-manager.test.mjs`: MIDI manager tests.
- `README.md`: user setup and controller guidance.

## Important Context
- The upstream Mixxx profile checked was `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixxxdj/mixxx/main/res/controllers/Numark-Party-Mix.midi.xml`; it identifies wheel-turn CC 6 on channels 1 and 2 and crossfader CC 8.
- The profile is for “Numark Party Mix,” not explicitly “Party Mix Live”; confirm compatibility before treating its mappings as definitive.

16: ## Highlights
17: 
18: - **Real jog-wheel scratching** — an AudioWorklet moves an interpolated read-head at signed rates, so reverse scratches, pitch bends, and touch-to-scratch feel immediate. A plain `AudioBufferSourceNode` cannot play backwards reliably.

20: - **Web MIDI input** — notes, CCs, pitch bend, aftertouch, program changes, and clock/sysex are parsed. A live monitor shows every incoming message and decoded jog delta.
21: - **Capacitive vs non-touch platters** — mapping a touch note marks the deck `CAPACITIVE`. In **AUTO** mode, capacitive decks scratch only while touched and pitch-nudge when released; non-touch decks auto-grab on rotation and release after the wheel stops.
22: - **Relative decoder modes** — 7-bit two's complement (`64 = 0`), offset, signed-bit, and absolute delta modes, plus adjustable ticks-per-revolution and sensitivity.

24: - **Virtual MIDI controller** — test the full MIDI path without hardware; it feeds the same parser as a physical controller.

## Objective
- Enable Numark Party Mix Live MIDI support in the existing playable ScratchLab browser DJ app.

## Requirements
- Make the change without clarification; note reasonable assumptions when finished.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks (viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use the existing MIDI Learn and mapping framework, with a controller-specific preset for easier setup.
- Use the upstream Mixxx Numark Party Mix mapping as a starter profile, but clearly describe Party Mix Live compatibility as an assumption, not confirmed hardware-specific verification.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected MIDI parsing, mapping, setup UI, auto-map wizard, tests, and README.
- Added exported `PARTY_MIX_LIVE_PRESET` to `js/midi.js`, using the upstream Party Mix controls and channels.
- Added `MidiManager.applyPreset()` to load a preset, clear decoder/button state, persist mappings, and notify listeners.

### Active
- Add UI action to apply the Party Mix Live profile.
- Add preset and manager tests; update setup guidance and README.
- Run tests and browser check, saving and reading a small JPEG screenshot.
